feed.title: HeatWatch
feed.subtitle: Where heat is breaking records, who it is reaching, what the rules are about to require, and what can be done about it.

entry.title: Southern California's heat wave ended close to forecast, running a day longer in the desert
entry.summary: The extreme heat warning covering most of Los Angeles and San Diego counties expired Thursday evening as expected. Desert areas and some San Diego County advisories ran through Friday instead. — Sources: National Weather Service San Diego, 7-8 October 2026 · National Weather Service Los Angeles, 7-8 October 2026

entry.title: California broke a decades-old heat record this week while wildfires burned nearby
entry.summary: San Diego Airport reached 40.6 degrees Celsius on 5 October, breaking a daily record that had stood since 1987, with more than 34 million people across California under heat alerts at the time. — Sources: Wire reporting via multiple outlets, 5 October 2026

entry.title: Singapore's air quality crossed into the unhealthy range two days before its own forecast
entry.summary: Fire hotspot counts in Sumatra, Indonesia eased slightly from 212 on 6 October to 188 on 7 October, but a wind shift pushed Singapore's air quality past the unhealthy threshold on the morning of 7 October. — Sources: National Environment Agency, Singapore, 7 October 2026

entry.title: Health professionals across five countries report rising heat harm to pregnant women and newborns
entry.summary: A survey of 1,000 maternal-health professionals across Australia, Brazil, India, the UK and Zimbabwe found 73% had seen a rise in heat-related pregnancy complications over the past five years and 76% a rise in impacts on newborn health, including dehydration, low birth weight and feeding difficulties. — Sources: Wellcome Trust survey, via Business Today, 6 October 2026

entry.title: South Africa's heat-stress rule now has a confirmed numeric trigger
entry.summary: A direct reading of South Africa's Physical Agents Regulations sets a heat-stress action level of 27 degrees Celsius WBGT and a time-weighted average exposure limit of 30 degrees Celsius WBGT on a one-hour basis. — Sources: Government Gazette No. 52226, Government Notice No. 5952, Department of Employment and Labour, South Africa, 6 March 2025
